catalog_quote: The tone system of Mundabli is characterized by four level tones and a number of contour tones. Tones are taken at their surface values. The only tonal process attested is low tone spread (see §3.4.2). Each syllable in Mundabli carries contrastive tone. Although nouns and verbs are nearly identical in their segmental setup, they differ considerably regarding their tonal behavior. While nouns generally retain their lexical tones, the tone patterns of verbs change depending on factors such as their syntactic position and the tense/mood/aspect in which they occur. ... The tone bearing unit in Mundabli is the syllable. There is no distinction in vowel length and the same tone combinations are possible in open and closed syllables. Mundabli has neither downstep nor phonetic downdrift. It is a “discrete level” language, i.e. tones are always realized at approximately the same pitch. ... The f…

audit.reasoning: The classification (tonal; no word-stress rule stated; domain not stated by the source) rests on the sole and current reference grammar (Voll 2017, 369 pp, open access), which we hold as PDF and text; the deciding quotation and the domain quotation are verbatim at the stated pages (pp. 15-16, p. 35). Glottolog lists no other grammar or phonology; web search turns up only vowel-phonetics papers (Faytak et al. 2023, 2024) and the Good et al. 2011 overview (downloaded; its Mundabli tone section, written with Voll, matches the grammar and is silent on stress). No better source exists or is likely to change the classification; no action needed.

sources.quote: 'There is evidence for four tone levels in Mundabli: low, mid, high and super-high ... The four tone levels can also combine to form various contour tones. There are three attested falling tones, mid-low, high-low and high-mid, but only one rising tone, from low to high ... Most nouns are monosyllabic'. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (only hit for 'stress' is 'It should be stressed that...').
sources.note: Independent (earlier, co-authored) statement of the Mundabli four-level tone system; downloaded and read, confirms tonal coding, adds nothing on stress.
